disposition_reason: Tables 2-3 and the Results text print mean, range and some per-product Cd, Co, As, Pb, Cr and Al concentrations for 20 infant formulas and 30 children food products from Gusau, Nigeria; the printed unit conflicts with the Discussion.

study.design: Market survey of 50 products: 20 infant formulas (8 milk-based, 6 cereal-based, 6 mixed; also grouped by age stage 0-6 (6), 6-12 (8), 12-24 months (6)) and 30 children food products; triplicate digestion
study.origin: locally and internationally produced (per product not stated)
study.market: supermarkets and pharmacies in Gusau, Zamfara State, Nigeria
study.method: MP-AES after HNO3/H2O2 (3:1) hotplate digestion of 1.0 g at 250 °C, diluted to 50 mL
study.qa: Acid-washed glassware; matrix spike recovery performed but recoveries not reported; no CRM

unresolved: Unit question: Tables 2-3 print µg/g (Cd about 2-2.6 µg/g = 2-2.6 mg/kg), but the Discussion states Cd values were within a 0.040 mg/kg limit and As only slightly above 0.1 mg/kg; values not converted to µg/kg until the unit is resolved.
Several means fall outside their printed ranges (e.g. cereal-based Cd 2.31 vs range 1.25-2.25).
Al rows for 0-6 months and milk-based formulas duplicate the Cr rows.
Children food product types and per-product values (Figure 1) are figure-only; the paper notes the high-metal products 'appeared to be plant-based'.
EDI table (Table 4) has implausible magnitudes (e.g. Cd EDI 0.394 mg/kg bw/day) and a Cd RfD printed as '0.001.51'; not used.
Physical form of formulas (powder) inferred from weighing 1.0 g samples and the Discussion's 'dry (as sold)' wording.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: As limit for infants quoted (EFSA and USFDA 2009)
